title: Geo flex warm-buffer allocator scenario log - NA/EU/APAC 2026-2028
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a scenario-driven forecast for regional GPU capacity (NA / EU / APAC) and an operational warm-buffer allocation strategy for 2026-2028. The goal is to codify triggers, buffer sizing, and staged rollouts so that Dedicated and Hosted capacity remain within SLA and cost targets during bursty adoption events.

TL;DR (two lines):
- Target warm-buffer = 8-15% of steady-state committed capacity per region; scale to 25% during onboarding surges or model rollouts.
- Prefer H100 for latency-sensitive model families, A100 for mixed workloads, and L4 for embedding/low-cost inference; plan a 30% L4 push for embeddings to reduce per-token cost.

Assumptions and defs (quick):
- GPU-unit: a normalized capacity unit (H100=1.0, A100=0.6, L4=0.15) used across planner calculations.
- Steady-state utilization target: 60-72% to balance cost and SLO headroom. Warm-buffer is extra capacity kept idle-or-warm for <5s spin-up.
- Warmpool warmup time: NA-east/NA-west: 8-12h for cold booting new nodes; APAC: allow 12-18h; EU: 10-14h.
- Backfill policy: use preemptible/spot for temporary bursts until sustained >72% for 3 consecutive days.

Methodology summary:
1) Base demand forecast: linear interpolation from usage telemetry (token/sec) and per-model kernel footprints; converted into GPU-units per region.
2) Risk-adjusted buffer: apply surge multipliers for events (product launches, model rollouts, SEV-driven fallbacks).
3) Timeline stitches: overlay vendor onboarding windows, contract commit dates, and travel time for private deployments.
4) Cost/quality tradeoffs: promote L4 offload for embedding-heavy tenants and hold H100 for low-latency chat models.

Notes on the table:
- Buffer % = base buffer target (8-12%) plus risk multiplier per region/event. APAC typically gets +3-6% for supplier lead-time risk.
- Provisioned GPU-units = Base + Buffer; we use round-up to nearest vendor tranche (typical tranche = 16-64 GPUs depending on vendor).

Region-specific operational guidance:
NA (east + west):
- Hot lanes: NA-east configured as primary for low-latency chat due to proximity to east-coast customers. Maintain a 20% warm-buffer during major model releases (canary -> prod).
- Fallback routing: in sustained NA-east strain >85% for 12+h, automatically route non-SLA traffic to NA-west with dynamic quantization set 16-bit. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-812 to track routing policy.

EU (central/west):
- Keep a tighter committed ratio (10% buffer) to reduce egress/cost; push embeddings to L4 pools in EU-west.
- EU legal/private deployments: separate warmpool with KMS integration; lead time for private racks = 6-10 weeks; add 6% contingency.

APAC (sg/jp):
- Supplier variance: expect longer vendor onboarding windows; hold larger warm-buffer (15-18%).
- Market growth sensitivity: APAC shows 2.5x variance in 6-month windows historically; plan to use cross-region burst to NA as fallback if latency permits.

Surge scenarios and triggers (operational runbook excerpt):
- Trigger A (Product launch / Internal rollout): +25% buffer for 7 days; procurement action: enable spot backfill and accelerate new tranche activation. Owner: Jonah Brooks. Runbook ticket: JIRA-INFRA-901.
- Trigger B (Model rollback causing regen storms): immediate 50% allocation to H100 warmpool for 72h; enable auto-throttle for embeddings. Owner: Mei Chen.
- Trigger C (Vendor-delivery delay > 2 weeks): escalate to procurement and enable cross-region shortfall lanes; target to cover 80% of missing GPU-units via spot/backfill within 48h.

Backfill policy details:
- Short bursts (<48h): use spot/GPU-spot instances across cloud vendors; prefer A100 spot with MIG where possible.
- Medium (48h-14d): combine spot + reserved burst from Dedicated pool; trigger cost approval for temporary commit.
- Long tail (>14d): accelerate committed purchases and negotiate vendor penalty clauses.

Open questions / follow-ups for next iteration:
- Validate per-tenant split of embedding vs. chat growth to reweight L4 adoption targets (owner: Diego Ramos).
- Confirm vendor tranche sizes for new H100 price bands (procurement: Talia Nguyen).
- Add more granular week-by-week warmpool spin-up times per cloud-zone (action: SRE-runbook 2.1).

Action table (short):
- Add cross-region routing feature flag to staging (owner: Jonah Brooks, due: 2026-03-05, linked: JIRA-INFRA-920)
- Run 72h sim of model rollout with mixed A100/H100 lanes (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-03-12, linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/567)
- Procurement: lock tranche pricing for H100 by 2026-04-01 (owner: Talia Nguyen, linked_artifact: JIRA-INFRA-789)

Scratch/notes to self (informal):
- Keep a small disposable L4 pool in each region for quick embedding routing tests.
- Slack thread references: #infra-capacity, see thread pinned message (search: \"warmpool ABI notes\").
- There's a partially-complete spreadsheet (high-fidelity) in CONF-InfraWarmpool-2026; this doc is intentionally scenario/log focused.

Versioning / provenance:
- This is an internal planning sheet, intermediate draft. Will be converted to a canonical playbook after stakeholder sign-off (expected Apr 2026).

Appendix (quick calc sample):
- Example: NA-east base 420 GPU-units in Jan-2026 (mixed H100/A100). With 10% buffer = 42 units. Provisioned rounding to vendor tranches -> 462 units. If steady-state utilization climbs to 78% for 24h, trigger medium backfill (48h-14d).
